title: Parenthetical Playbook: A Kid-Friendly Guide to Acting’s Whispered Secrets
author: Corey Ralston

body:
In the realm of acting, parentheticals are like secret whispers that help young actors bring their characters to life. They are tiny clues hiding in the script, telling you how to say your lines. For parents and budding stars, understanding these hidden treasures can make the journey of acting even more thrilling!

Let’s break down these whispered secrets with some examples, shall we?

  1. Emotional Hints:

    • Line: (excitedly) "Guess what, I won the spelling bee!"

    • This is a nudge to sound super excited like you can hardly contain your joy.

  2. Physical Action:

    • Line: (rolling eyes) "Oh sure, another alien invasion."

    • Here, while you say the line, you roll your eyes as if you've heard this a million times before.

  3. Volume Modulation:

    • Line: (whispering) "I think there's a monster under my bed."

    • This whispering hint tells you to keep your voice low as if sharing a scary secret.

  4. Pacing:

    • Line: (hurriedly) "Hurry, the train is leaving!"

    • The hint is to say the line quickly, like you're in a big rush.

  5. Vocal Quality:

    • Line: (sarcastically) "Oh great, it's raining on our parade."

    • Here, a touch of sarcasm should lace your voice, showing how you feel about the rain.

  6. Beat:

    • Line: (pausing) "I... I don't know what to say."

    • This clue tells you to take a little break, showing you're at a loss for words.

  7. Character-Specific Instructions:

    • Line: (as a pirate) "Arr matey, the treasure be ours!"

    • This is a fun one, telling you to channel your inner pirate as you celebrate the treasure.

Parentheticals are like secret keys, helping our young actors unlock the magic in their performance. They add a splash of color, a dash of emotion, and a sprinkle of authenticity to every scene. So, the next time you or your young star bump into these whispered secrets in a script, get ready to play, explore, and shine brighter on the stage or screen!
